sky.yt_title: Why This Skyscraper Was Fixed at Night #shorts
sky.yt_desc:
A student's homework showed that a brand-new New York tower could blow over in a storm, so welders fixed it in secret, every night, while a hurricane was coming.

Would you have told the people inside? A or B 👇

Sources:
• 99% Invisible, "Structural Integrity": https://99percentinvisible.org/episode/structural-integrity/
• The Real Deal, "How a student saved Citicorp Center": https://therealdeal.com/2014/04/17/how-student-saved-citicorp-center-from-potential-collapse/
• Wikipedia, Citicorp Center engineering crisis: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citicorp_Center_engineering_crisis

lemon.yt_title: The Robber Who Trusted Lemon Juice #shorts
lemon.yt_desc:
A man robbed two banks with no mask because he believed lemon juice made his face invisible to cameras. His mistake ended up inspiring a famous psychology study.

Would you have trusted that photo? A or B 👇

Sources:
• Wikipedia, 1995 Greater Pittsburgh bank robberies: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_Greater_Pittsburgh_bank_robberies
• Kruger & Dunning (1999), "Unskilled and Unaware of It", Journal of Personality and Social Psychology: https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.77.6.1121

Music: "Sneaky Snitch", "Volatile Reaction", "Fluffing a Duck", "Carefree" by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), licensed under CC BY 4.0. Sound effects: CC0 (OpenGameArt).
Animated story, told by Oddwick 🕯️

slugs.yt_title: How Garden Slugs Became Gas Alarms #shorts
slugs.yt_desc:
In World War I, a museum scientist noticed that garden slugs shut their breathing hole and scrunch up when the air turns bad, so the US Army took them to the trenches as mustard-gas alarms.

Slug or dog: which would you trust? A or B 👇

Sources:
• UC Agriculture and Natural Resources, "Slug: Garden Pest and War Hero" (citing the Smithsonian Institution Archives): https://ucanr.edu/blog/under-solano-sun/article/slug-garden-pest-and-war-hero
• Smithsonian, "How did animals (even slugs) serve in World War I?": https://si.edu/object/how-did-animals-even-slugs-serve-world-war-i:posts_7ec8765541a1cb6d6c3ff459cd89314f

The sergeant's lines are a dramatized retelling; the slug facts are from the sources above.
